# obsidian-second-brain-contabil

> A slimmed fork of obsidian-second-brain (https://github.com/eugeniughelbur/obsidian-second-brain, MIT) for accounting offices: persistent memory for Claude Code and Codex in an Obsidian vault. Every note is designed for AI retrieval, not human reading. An evolution of Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern (https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f): every source updates existing pages instead of just appending, and contradictions reconcile automatically. 38 commands span vault management and thinking tools, plus optional local semantic search (Ollama on the same machine), a write-time AI-first validator hook, an opt-in background agent and a `/create-command` interview flow. This fork removes every feature that sends vault or conversation content to a third-party service.

## What this is

An open-source skill (MIT license) for Obsidian users who use an AI CLI as their primary interface to their own knowledge. It treats the vault as a knowledge base optimized for AI retrieval rather than human reading. Every note follows an AI-first design rule: self-contained context, "For future agent" preamble, rich machine-readable frontmatter, recency markers per claim, sources preserved verbatim, mandatory wikilinks, and confidence levels.

The skill is platform-neutral. The same 38 commands run in Claude Code, OpenAI Codex CLI (native Agent Skills), OpenCode and Google Antigravity (via the unified `.agents/skills/` Agent Skills build). One codebase compiles into all four via `bash scripts/build.sh`.

Owner: Eugeniu Ghelbur (AI Automation Engineer, AI Tooling Engineer, AI Educator). Questions or consulting: e.ghelbur@gmail.com or LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/in/eugeniu-ghelbur/

Author links: GitHub https://github.com/eugeniughelbur | The AI Operator (blog) https://theaioperator.io | X https://x.com/eugeniu_ghelbur | LinkedIn https://www.linkedin.com/in/eugeniu-ghelbur/

## Crew: one logbook for Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Grok Bot

Crew (v0.18.0, `/crew`) is a shared job log for AI coding agents. After every job, an agent writes one line (time, agent, area, outcome, evidence) to a plain markdown file. Before an agent answers, its hooks hand it the lines the others added since it last looked, so Claude Code knows what Codex did without the user pasting context. Agents can also leave each other lessons; a lesson becomes a rule in that agent's rules file only when the human runs `keep`.

- Works without Obsidian: any folder (`~/crew`), or `wiki/team/` inside a vault.
- Setup: `/crew setup` merges read hooks for Claude Code and Codex (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit) and Cursor (sessionStart, postToolUse), and prints a profile block for Grok Bot.
- Safety: every read is framed as records, not instructions; inputs are cleaned to one line; writes are locked and atomic; Crew runs no background loop.
- One standard-library Python file (`scripts/crew.py`), Python 3.10+.
- Shared agent memory is not new. Crew's own parts: Grok Bot on the same team, lessons gated by a human keep, and no background loop.

## Why people use it

- Claude sessions start from zero every time. This skill solves that by storing context in the Obsidian vault and letting the AI read, write, and reason over it across sessions.
- Notes accumulate unconnected. This skill propagates every write across people, projects, kanban boards, and daily notes automatically.
- Vaults are usually optimized for humans browsing in Obsidian. This skill treats the vault as an AI knowledge graph: the next compatible agent (Claude, Codex, or another client) is the primary reader.

## How this extends Karpathy's LLM Wiki pattern

Andrej Karpathy described an LLM Wiki pattern: drop sources into a folder, have an LLM read them, create wiki pages, and cross-reference entities and concepts so future questions are answered from the wiki rather than a fresh search. Reference: https://gist.github.com/karpathy/442a6bf555914893e9891c11519de94f

obsidian-second-brain implements this pattern and extends it on these axes:

1. New sources rewrite existing pages instead of appending. When you ingest an article about a person already in your vault, the person's page gets updated. Stale claims get replaced. The vault stays current automatically.
2. Contradictions get reconciled, not just flagged. The /obsidian-reconcile command finds conflicts between notes and resolves them by checking sources, dates, and confidence levels.
3. Patterns get surfaced without prompting. The /obsidian-synthesize command scans the vault for unnamed recurring themes and writes synthesis pages on its own.
4. Maintenance is a command away. /obsidian-health, /obsidian-reconcile and /obsidian-learn keep the vault consistent.
5. Notes are written for AI retrieval. Every note has a "For future agent" preamble, machine-readable frontmatter, mandatory wikilinks, and recency markers per claim. Karpathy's pattern produces human-readable wiki pages; this produces AI-first notes.
6. Write-time enforcement. A `PostToolUse` hook (`validate-ai-first.sh`) inspects every Write or Edit on a markdown file inside the vault and warns when the AI-first rule is broken (missing frontmatter fields, missing preamble, broken YAML). The vault stays AI-first because every write is checked, not because the AI remembers all seven rules every time.

If Karpathy's LLM Wiki is a knowledge base you maintain with an LLM, obsidian-second-brain is a knowledge base that maintains itself across multiple AI CLIs.

## The 38 commands (organized by category)

**Vault (14)** - daily writing, capture, find, kanban, recurring obligations, recall:
obsidian-board, obsidian-board-hygiene, obsidian-capture, obsidian-checkin, obsidian-daily, obsidian-find, obsidian-log, obsidian-person, obsidian-project, obsidian-recap, obsidian-recurring, obsidian-save, obsidian-task, obsidian-world.

**Thinking (14)** - synthesis, decisions, learning, reviews, panels, discovery, brainstorming:
obsidian-brainstorm, obsidian-challenge, obsidian-connect, obsidian-decide, obsidian-distill, obsidian-emerge, obsidian-graduate, obsidian-learn, obsidian-panel, obsidian-reconcile, obsidian-review, obsidian-synthesize, idea-discovery, vault-deep-synthesis.

**Ingest (1)** - bring local files or web articles into the vault:
obsidian-ingest.

**Meta (9)** - vault setup, health, structure, search quality, agent coordination, tooling:
crew, obsidian-export, obsidian-health, obsidian-init, obsidian-merge, obsidian-reindex, obsidian-retrieval-eval, obsidian-visualize, create-command.

Plus hook scripts: `obsidian-bg-agent.sh` (PostCompact session propagation, opt-in), `validate-ai-first.sh` (write-time AI-first enforcement incl. secret detection) and opt-in `obsidian-recall.py`.

## Multi-platform architecture

The repo is structured around a build-time adapter pattern:

- `commands/` - 38 platform-neutral source files with frontmatter declaring `description`, `category` (vault/thinking/research/meta; `research` is the label used by obsidian-ingest), `triggers_en` (natural-language trigger phrases), and an optional `exclude` (per-platform opt-out).
- `adapters/lib.sh` - shared parsing, path rewriting, tool-name neutralization, grouped routing-table emission, multilingual trigger emission.
- `adapters/claude-code/adapter.sh` - identity copy (Claude Code's slash-command format matches the source).
- `adapters/codex-cli/adapter.sh` - emits native Codex Agent Skills plus a thin `AGENTS.md`.
- `adapters/opencode/adapter.sh` - emits `AGENTS.md`. Commands under `.opencode/commands/`.
- `adapters/agent-skills/adapter.sh` - one `.agents/skills/` tree for Codex CLI, OpenCode and Antigravity.
- `scripts/build.sh` - orchestrator. Run with `--platform <name>` for one platform or no argument for all four.

Output goes to `dist/<platform>/` (gitignored). Each `dist/<platform>/INSTALL.md` documents the install path for that CLI.

## /create-command interview flow

`/create-command` lets users build new commands without editing markdown. It runs a conversation: intent, naming (kebab-case, validates no collision), category, trigger phrases, behavior steps, AI-first compliance gate, external API declaration, then writes the file.

## Stack

- Python 3.10+ with uv (dependencies: python-dotenv, pyyaml)
- Settings stored machine-locally at `~/.config/obsidian-second-brain/.env` with permissions 600
- bash 3.x compatible adapters (no associative arrays, no bashisms)
- No network calls from the scripts by default. Semantic search uses Ollama on localhost; the `openai` embedding backend is opt-in and sends note text off the machine.

## The AI-first vault rule

The single most important design principle. Every note Claude writes must satisfy seven rules:

1. Self-contained context: each note explains itself; a future agent may pull it via search with no surrounding context
2. "For future agent" preamble: 2-3 sentence summary so the next agent can decide relevance in 10 seconds before parsing the note
3. Rich consistent frontmatter: type, date, tags, ai-first: true, plus type-specific fields per the schemas in `references/ai-first-rules.md`
4. Recency markers per claim: "Mem0 raised $24M (as of 2026-04, mem0.ai)" so future-Claude knows what to verify
5. Sources preserved verbatim: every external claim has its source URL inline
6. Cross-links mandatory: every person, project, idea, decision uses `[[wikilinks]]` so the graph is traversable
7. Confidence levels: `stated | high | medium | speculation` where applicable

The rule lives in `_CLAUDE.md` Section 0 of every vault using this skill, and in `references/ai-first-rules.md` (the canonical specification with frontmatter schemas and preamble templates per note type).

A `PostToolUse` hook (`hooks/validate-ai-first.sh`) enforces this at write time: it fires after every Write/Edit on a markdown file inside `OBSIDIAN_VAULT_PATH` and warns on missing fields or preamble. The original write is not reverted; the warning surfaces on stderr so the AI can repair the note in the same turn.

## Install

### Claude Code (default - plugin marketplace)

```
/plugin marketplace add Mouraovicente/obsidian-second-brain-contabil
/plugin install obsidian-second-brain@obsidian-second-brain-contabil
```

(Classic alternative: clone to ~/.claude/skills/obsidian-second-brain and run scripts/setup.sh.)

### Codex CLI / OpenCode / Google Antigravity (unified Agent Skills build)

```bash
git clone https://github.com/Mouraovicente/obsidian-second-brain-contabil
cd obsidian-second-brain
bash scripts/build.sh --platform agent-skills
npx skills add ./dist/agent-skills -a codex -a opencode -a antigravity   # or cp -R dist/agent-skills/skills/. <vault>/.agents/skills/
```

To update a copied build later: `bash scripts/update-vault-integration.sh --vault /path/to/vault` (guarded: fast-forward pull, smoke-test gate, backup + rollback).

## Common questions

### Do I need API keys to use this?
No. None of the 38 commands needs an API key.

### Does this work with Obsidian Sync?
Yes. The skill writes to your vault as standard markdown files. Obsidian Sync, iCloud, Syncthing, and Git-based sync all work without modification.

### What is the AI-first design rule?
The principle that vault notes are written for future agents to retrieve and reason over, not for human reading. Notes have machine-readable structure, recency markers, mandatory wikilinks, and source URLs preserved verbatim. See `references/ai-first-rules.md`.

### Is this safe to run on my existing vault?
Yes. The skill never deletes or modifies notes destructively without explicit confirmation. Existing notes are left as-is. New notes follow the AI-first rule. `/obsidian-health` flags pre-AI-first notes so you can update them on your own schedule.

### How do Claude Code and Codex share memory?
Through Crew's logbook. Claude Code and Codex read new lines through their SessionStart and UserPromptSubmit hooks. The files are plain markdown in `~/crew` or a vault's `wiki/team/`.

### Can a log line give my agent orders?
Crew frames every read as records, not instructions, and cleans each field to one line. Framing helps a model separate data from orders; it cannot guarantee it. Crew runs no background loop, so nothing acts on a line by itself.
